prov_p105.name: Bạch Hoa
prov_p105.lore: Coastal forest climbing from the sea into steep hills, its lower slopes a pied grove of white birch and black stumps left by the fire of 548. Its people strip birch bark for writing sheets and boxes and fish the coast. The fire's dead town, Hỏa Tẫn Trấn, still stands burned on the shore.

prov_p106.name: Thanh Tùng
prov_p106.lore: River forest in the hills west of the palace, around the memorial pines of Thanh Tùng Thôn. Its people are woodsmen and river folk, many of them children of Hổ Khiếu's survivors. They neither cut nor tap the old pines of the forest above the village.

prov_p107.name: Tùng Phong
prov_p107.lore: High river forest in the south of the pine sea, where Vạn Hác Viện's students practise among the villagers. Its people are woodsmen, hunters and zither-string twisters. Striped tigers hold the ridge above, and the wind strings warn the hamlet when the wind turns toward it.

prov_p32.name: Tùng Gian
prov_p32.lore: The small river mouth around Tùng Gian Thành, Tùng Đào's first city and port. Its land is all city, harbour and pine grove, with a clear spring running over the stones by the river. Timber, resin and pilgrims pass through its moon gate.

prov_p46.name: Tùng Hạ
prov_p46.lore: Wide pine sea along the road to the palace, with Tùng Hạ Thị's ring market at its heart. Caravans, woodcutters and pilgrims fill its roads, and wolves follow the caravans in hard winters. Since 1191 the new Tuần Tùng Đường keeps the road watch from the hills above the market.

prov_p60.name: Lộc Minh
prov_p60.lore: Low river forest and coast around Lộc Minh Trấn, the carvers' town held by Lãng Đào Môn. Its people carve, ferry and fish. Deep in its pines lie the clawed walls of Hổ Khiếu Trấn, and giant otters hold the river bend below the town.

prov_p61.name: Cổ Độ
prov_p61.lore: Hill forest and bamboo along the southern river around Cổ Độ Thành and its ferry stair. Its people ferry, smith and drag the old chain links of Thiết Tỏa Quan from the river. A bamboo spirit vein lies in the hills, and an older iron town stands empty upslope.

prov_tung_dao.name: Tùng Đào
prov_tung_dao.lore: The palace ridge and the endless pines around it, rising to a thousand metres. Its people are the palace's servants, foresters and the families of outer disciples, and pilgrims climb the ridge only to listen. A spirit vein of wood and water qi below the gallery is where new disciples first learn to hear the pine waves.

prov_van_hac.name: Vạn Hác
prov_van_hac.lore: Ravine-broken pine forest climbing into high mountain, around Vạn Hác Viện and its pillar pavilion. Zither makers, malachite miners and the academy's students are its people. The rockfall that buried Cầm Tượng Trấn in 1012 still scars one ravine wall.

prov_r4_1.name: Hàn Than Hoang
prov_r4_1.lore: Tundra, bog and thin forest on the northern coast, with cold shoals offshore. No one lives here now. The fallen pavilion of Vọng Triều Các stands on the shore, and a spring of water qi rises in the woods behind.

prov_r4_10.name: Tùng Mặc
prov_r4_10.lore: Inland pine forest in the north of the pine sea, where villagers burn pine to soot and press it into ink cakes. Tùng Mặc ink is sold in every sect library of the north. The misty wood beside the village gives the softest soot.

prov_r4_11.name: Phạt Mộc
prov_r4_11.lore: Pine forest rising from the coastal lowland into hills. Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters and send the logs down to Tùng Gian Thành. A spirit vein of budding wood qi lies in its hills.

prov_r4_12.name: Tùng Mật
prov_r4_12.lore: Forested hills climbing toward high mountain west of the palace. Its villagers keep bees in log hives and sell dark pine honey on the palace road. Above them a cloud forest climbs nearly to a thousand metres.

prov_r4_13.name: Hương Khuẩn
prov_r4_13.lore: Forest and rocky high ground on the western edge of the pine sea. Its people gather and dry fragrant mushrooms that grow on fallen pine. Black leopards den on the crags, and gatherers go out in pairs.

prov_r4_14.name: Cát Chi
prov_r4_14.lore: Forest rising from low valleys into steep hills. Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish, under foresters' rules on how many cuts a tree may bear. A heavy vein of earth qi lies under the hill above the village.

prov_r4_15.name: Hương Khách
prov_r4_15.lore: Hill forest south of the palace ridge, on the pilgrims' road. Its village lives by lodging and feeding pilgrims, who climb on to the ridge to listen to the pines. The wood above the village sounds so like the sea that pilgrims sometimes stop there and go no further.

prov_r4_16.name: Tiều Phu
prov_r4_16.lore: High forest and rock above the ravines, home to woodsmen who sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. White apes hold the ridge above a thousand metres. The ginseng town of Thải Tham Trấn was driven out by those apes in 979.

prov_r4_17.name: Dương Lan
prov_r4_17.lore: High forest climbing to bare rock above a thousand metres. Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and on the high meadows, and pen them in dry-stone folds at night. Dwarf pines crouch on the summits where nothing else grows.

prov_r4_18.name: Phù Mộc
prov_r4_18.lore: River forest south-east of the palace, its river carrying driftwood down from the mountains. Villagers gather the driftwood and float logs to the lowlands. The red-barked pines above the river are among the oldest in the pine sea.

prov_r4_19.name: Biên Trúc
prov_r4_19.lore: High forest where the first bamboo of the south creeps in among the pines. Villagers weave bamboo fences, baskets and mats for the markets of Cổ Độ. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a still grove on the slope.

prov_r4_2.name: Liệp Hồ
prov_r4_2.lore: Forest, tundra and bog on the northern coast. Its people hunt foxes and trap for furs and fish the coast in summer. Grey wolves hold a knoll inland and take a share of every winter's catch.

prov_r4_20.name: Bán Sơn
prov_r4_20.lore: Forested mountain climbing to over sixteen hundred metres south-east of the palace. Its village sits halfway up and lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. The peak's metal qi draws Tùng Đào's disciples in summer.

prov_r4_21.name: Vân Ổ
prov_r4_21.lore: High mountain and forest on the eastern edge, often sunk in cloud. Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. A slender green-grey peak rises above the hollow like a hairpin.

prov_r4_22.name: Lạc Thạch
prov_r4_22.lore: High forest under crags that shed stones every spring. Villagers quarry the fallen stone and carve millstones. The avalanche that buried Hàn Thạch Trấn in 1151 is still remembered in every house.

prov_r4_23.name: Thảo Pha
prov_r4_23.lore: Forested hills opening into grassy slopes in the south. Its people graze cattle on the slopes and cut yew in the woods for bows. It is the warmest land in the pine sea.

prov_r4_24.name: Thạch Tỉnh
prov_r4_24.lore: Forest and high rock in the south-east, its village gathered around a deep stone well. Its people herd goats and dig a little copper from the hill. Giant flying squirrels glide over the crags at dusk.

prov_r4_25.name: Hôi Nham Lĩnh
prov_r4_25.lore: Bare high mountain near the border of the heart, rising to over eighteen hundred metres. No one lives here but Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch and the miners of the grey iron mine. The rock is grey like the pines on the summit.

prov_r4_26.name: Tửu Phường
prov_r4_26.lore: River forest in the far south, where villagers brew pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. Venom hornets nest in the woods behind. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

prov_r4_27.name: Quan Hạ
prov_r4_27.lore: High mountain, forest and grassland around the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan. Its village lives by goats and the iron mine above. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples here to see what breaking the peace cost.

prov_r4_3.name: Thủ Mộ
prov_r4_3.lore: Quiet northern forest around the fallen temple of Khô Mộc Tự. Its villagers keep the temple's graves and gather firewood and fungus. The forest beside it is so still that birdsong carries for a mile.

prov_r4_4.name: Hắc Nhĩ
prov_r4_4.lore: Damp northern forest where black wood-ear fungus grows thick on fallen logs. Its people gather and dry it for the markets of Tùng Gian. The forest is green and misty even in late autumn.

prov_r4_5.name: Tùng Hoa
prov_r4_5.lore: Inland pine forest that turns the air yellow with pollen each spring. Villagers collect the pollen for cakes and medicine. A spirit vein of wood qi lies under a wave of green hills.

prov_r4_6.name: Mộc Tập
prov_r4_6.lore: River lowland in the north-east of the pine sea, where the timber of the north is gathered and sold. Mộc Tập Trấn holds a timber fair each spring. Dawn redwoods grow along the river.

prov_r4_7.name: Lâu Thuyền
prov_r4_7.lore: Coastal forest whose town builds ships from straight pine. Lâu Thuyền Trấn launches Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its mast pines are guarded by foresters.

prov_r4_8.name: Thải Tân
prov_r4_8.lore: Inland forest of mixed pine and broadleaf. Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. It is the plainest land in the pine sea, and its people are proud of it.

prov_r4_9.name: Triều Thanh
prov_r4_9.lore: Coastal forest dipping below the sea in places. Its fishers listen to the tide from their houses. The sea wind bends the pines along the shore.

prov_p105_beast_lair_1.name: Ngân Hồ Cương
prov_p105_beast_lair_1.look: A birch-crowned knoll riddled with fox earths, silver-grey fur caught on the brambles around every hole.
prov_p105_beast_lair_1.lore: Silver foxes den here, clever enough to rob the bark-strippers' lunches. Villagers say a fox that steals from you brings luck if you let it go.

prov_p105_ruin_2.name: Hỏa Tẫn Trấn
prov_p105_ruin_2.look: On the coast, charred posts and blackened stone hearths stand among young birches, the ground still dark with old ash.
prov_p105_ruin_2.lore: A timber town that burned with the forest in the great fire of 548. Its survivors moved inland, and the birches that grew over the burn gave Bạch Hoa its name.

prov_p106_forest_1.name: Cổ Cái Lâm
prov_p106_forest_1.look: Old pines with vast flat crowns that touch overhead, leaving the forest floor dim and soft with needles.
prov_p106_forest_1.lore: These are the oldest pines near Thanh Tùng, and the villagers neither cut nor tap them. The survivors of Hổ Khiếu say their dead walk here.

prov_p107_beast_lair_1.name: Ban Hổ Lĩnh
prov_p107_beast_lair_1.look: A pine ridge above Tùng Phong, its bark clawed at head height and its paths marked with great striped hairs.
prov_p107_beast_lair_1.lore: Tigers hold the ridge, and when the wind turns toward the hamlet the wind strings hum a warning. Vạn Hác's students say a well-played zither keeps them away.

prov_p32_spirit_vein_1.name: Thạch Thượng Tuyền
prov_p32_spirit_vein_1.look: A clear spring runs over flat river stones under pines just outside Tùng Gian Thành, and at night the moon shines through the pines on it.
prov_p32_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring, named for Vương Duy's line of the clear spring that flows over the stones. Townsfolk fetch its water for the Night of a Thousand Pines.

prov_p46_spirit_vein_1.name: Tùng Âm Mạch
prov_p46_spirit_vein_1.look: On a hill above the ring market, a stand of pines sings in even the lightest wind, and the ground under them is warm.
prov_p46_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under these pines, and pilgrims to the palace stop here to listen first. Tùng Đào's disciples say it is the vein that makes the pines sing.

prov_p46_minor_seat_p.name: Tuần Tùng Đường
prov_p46_minor_seat_p.look: On a pine-covered hill above the road, a long timber hall with a watchtower at each end, bows racked under the eaves and wolf pelts on the walls.
prov_p46_minor_seat_p.lore: Tuần Tùng Đường is a young sect of road wardens sworn to Tùng Đào Cung, founded after wolves followed the caravans to Tùng Hạ Thị in 1190. Its wardens guard the caravans through the pine sea with staff and bow, and take their fee in coin and salt.

sect.name: Tuần Tùng Đường
sect.craft: road wardens and caravan guards; staff and bow arts

prov_p60_beast_lair_1.name: Cự Thát Chử
prov_p60_beast_lair_1.look: Low sandbars in a river bend below Lộc Minh, littered with fish bones and slick slides into the water.
prov_p60_beast_lair_1.lore: Otters as long as boats hunt the river bend and steal from the ferry nets. Lãng Đào's ferrymen toss them a fish as they pass, and the otters let them by.

prov_p61_spirit_vein_1.name: Trúc Căn Mạch
prov_p61_spirit_vein_1.look: A bamboo grove on a hillside above Cổ Độ grows taller and greener than any around it, its stems creaking in the still air.
prov_p61_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the grove, and its bamboo grows a man's height in a night in spring. The smiths of Cổ Độ cut their tongs' handles from it.

prov_p61_ruin_2.name: Luyện Thiết Trấn
prov_p61_ruin_2.look: On a hillside above the river, the slumped stone bellies of old smelting furnaces stand among pines, slag heaps grown over with moss.
prov_p61_ruin_2.lore: This town smelted iron for Tùng Đào, and its furnaces made much of the chain for Thiết Tỏa Quan. After the War of the Pivot the palace stopped buying iron, and within a generation the town was empty.

prov_tung_dao_spirit_vein_1.name: Thính Đào Nhãn
prov_tung_dao_spirit_vein_1.gloss: Eye Where One Hears the Waves
prov_tung_dao_spirit_vein_1.look: Just below the long gallery, a round hollow among the pines holds a still pool, and the sound of the pines falls into it like surf.
prov_tung_dao_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Wood and Water qi rises in the pool. New disciples of Tùng Đào sit by it to learn to hear the pine waves before they are taught a single art.

prov_van_hac_forest_1.name: Bích Hác Sâm
prov_van_hac_forest_1.look: High on the ravine rims, a dark forest of fir and pine clings to the edges, its roots hanging over the drops.
prov_van_hac_forest_1.lore: Vạn Hác's students climb here to play into the ravines and hear the echoes return. Zither makers take their soundboard wood only from trees that have fallen into the ravines.

prov_van_hac_ruin_2.name: Cầm Tượng Trấn
prov_van_hac_ruin_2.look: At the foot of a ravine wall, broken workshop roofs and half-carved zither bodies lie under a slope of fallen rock.
prov_van_hac_ruin_2.lore: Zither makers settled here to serve Vạn Hác Viện soon after its founding. In 1012 the ravine wall gave way and buried half the town, and the survivors moved to the academy rim.

prov_r4_1_spirit_vein_1.name: Lãnh Triều Tuyền
prov_r4_1_spirit_vein_1.look: In the woods behind the shore a cold spring wells up into a stone basin, its water salt-cold and smelling faintly of the sea.
prov_r4_1_spirit_vein_1.lore: A spirit vein of Water qi feeds the spring, its flow strongest at the high tide. The tide-watchers of Vọng Triều Các drew their water from it for two centuries.

prov_r4_1_ruin_2.name: Vọng Triều Các
prov_r4_1_ruin_2.look: On a bare shore, the stone base of a pavilion faces the sea, its steps running down into the water.
prov_r4_1_ruin_2.lore: A small sect of water arts that cultivated the rhythm of the tide. Its last master walked into the winter sea in 468 to cultivate the tide and never came back; within two years its disciples went to Tùng Đào Cung.

prov_r4_10_village_1.name: Tùng Mặc Thôn
prov_r4_10_village_1.look: Low sheds with long clay flues climb a slope, black soot coating every roof, and rows of ink cakes dry on boards in the shade.
prov_r4_10_village_1.lore: Villagers burn pine in long flues, scrape the soot and pound it with glue into ink cakes. Tùng Mặc ink is sold in every sect library of the north.

prov_r4_10_forest_2.name: U Lam Lâm
prov_r4_10_forest_2.look: A pine wood in a hollow where mist lies all morning, the trunks fading into grey.
prov_r4_10_forest_2.lore: The ink-makers say pine from the misty wood gives the softest soot. Travellers lose the path here easily.

prov_r4_11_village_1.name: Phạt Mộc Thôn
prov_r4_11_village_1.look: A woodcutters' village with log slides running downhill and stacks of marked logs by the road.
prov_r4_11_village_1.lore: Its woodcutters fell only trees marked by Tùng Đào's foresters. A tree cut without a mark costs the cutter a year's work.

prov_r4_11_spirit_vein_2.name: Manh Nha Mạch
prov_r4_11_spirit_vein_2.look: A hillside where young pines grow thick and fast, and the snow melts weeks before anywhere else.
prov_r4_11_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi wakes the hill early each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters gather seedlings here for replanting the cut slopes.

prov_r4_12_village_1.name: Tùng Mật Thôn
prov_r4_12_village_1.look: Hollow-log hives hang in the pines around a small village, and the air hums with bees.
prov_r4_12_village_1.lore: Its beekeepers make a dark, resinous pine honey sold on the palace road. They say their bees learn the pine waves too.

prov_r4_12_forest_2.name: Lăng Vân Lâm
prov_r4_12_forest_2.look: On high slopes, tall firs rise through drifting cloud, their tops showing above it like masts.
prov_r4_12_forest_2.lore: The forest is often above the clouds, and Tùng Đào's disciples climb to cultivate in its thin air. The beekeepers will not go higher than its edge.

prov_r4_13_village_1.name: Hương Khuẩn Thôn
prov_r4_13_village_1.look: Racks of drying mushrooms line every house, and the village smells of earth and woodsmoke.
prov_r4_13_village_1.lore: Its people gather mushrooms from fallen pine and dry them for the markets. They go out in pairs, for the leopards above.

prov_r4_13_beast_lair_2.name: Huyền Báo Nhai
prov_r4_13_beast_lair_2.look: A dark crag in the forest, its ledges strewn with bones and its rock marked with black hairs.
prov_r4_13_beast_lair_2.lore: Black leopards den in its caves and hunt the forest by night. The mushroom gatherers carry bells to warn them off.

prov_r4_14_village_1.name: Cát Chi Thôn
prov_r4_14_village_1.look: A valley village whose pines bear neat cuts above clay cups, and pots of golden resin cool on the doorsteps.
prov_r4_14_village_1.lore: Its people tap pine resin for incense and varnish. The foresters count the cuts on every tree each autumn.

prov_r4_14_spirit_vein_2.name: Hậu Thổ Mạch
prov_r4_14_spirit_vein_2.look: On a steep hillside, a broad shelf of dark earth holds no trees, only thick grass and a few heavy boulders.
prov_r4_14_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Earth qi runs under the shelf, heavy and slow. Tùng Đào's disciples who lean to earth come here, though few of them do.

prov_r4_15_village_1.name: Hương Khách Thôn
prov_r4_15_village_1.look: A village of inns and tea stalls on the pilgrims' road, incense smoke drifting from every door.
prov_r4_15_village_1.lore: It lives by lodging pilgrims bound for the palace ridge. Innkeepers sell pine cones as keepsakes.

prov_r4_15_forest_2.name: Hải Vận Lâm
prov_r4_15_forest_2.look: A pine wood on a hill whose crowns roar in the wind exactly like surf on a beach.
prov_r4_15_forest_2.lore: Pilgrims who stop here sometimes never go on to the palace, saying they have heard enough. Tùng Đào's disciples call it the near sea.

prov_r4_16_village_1.name: Tiều Phu Thôn
prov_r4_16_village_1.look: A hamlet of log houses on a high slope, firewood stacked to the eaves.
prov_r4_16_village_1.lore: Its woodsmen sell firewood and charcoal to Vạn Hác. They keep clear of the white apes above.

prov_r4_16_beast_lair_2.name: Bạch Viên Lĩnh
prov_r4_16_beast_lair_2.look: A high ridge of fir and rock where white-furred apes sit on the boulders, watching the valley.
prov_r4_16_beast_lair_2.lore: White apes hold the ridge and throw stones at anyone who climbs. They drove out the ginseng diggers of Thải Tham Trấn in 979.

prov_r4_16_ruin_3.name: Thải Tham Trấn
prov_r4_16_ruin_3.look: On a high slope, the stone walls of a small town are tumbled and grown with ferns, and dug pits pock the ground around it.
prov_r4_16_ruin_3.lore: Ginseng diggers built this town when the roots were plentiful. As the ginseng ran out they dug higher, into the apes' ridge, and in 979 the apes drove them out.

prov_r4_17_village_1.name: Dương Lan Thôn
prov_r4_17_village_1.look: A high village of dry-stone sheepfolds, goats and sheep spread over the meadows above it.
prov_r4_17_village_1.lore: Its shepherds graze goats and sheep in the clearings and high meadows and pen them at night against the apes and leopards. They make hard cheese for Vạn Hác.

prov_r4_17_forest_2.name: Ải Tùng Lâm
prov_r4_17_forest_2.look: On bare high rock, a low forest of dwarf pines no taller than a man crouches against the wind.
prov_r4_17_forest_2.lore: The dwarf pines are said to be as old as the palace. Shepherds shelter their flocks among them in storms.

prov_r4_18_village_1.name: Phù Mộc Thôn
prov_r4_18_village_1.look: A river village whose beaches are heaped with driftwood, bleached and sorted by size, and log booms tied along the bank.
prov_r4_18_village_1.lore: Its people gather driftwood from the river and float logs downstream to the lowland towns. They build their houses only from wood the river has brought them.

prov_r4_18_forest_2.name: Xích Bì Lâm
prov_r4_18_forest_2.look: A wood of old pines with bright red bark, glowing in the evening sun.
prov_r4_18_forest_2.lore: These are among the oldest pines in the pine sea. Tùng Đào's foresters mark none for cutting.

prov_r4_19_village_1.name: Biên Trúc Thôn
prov_r4_19_village_1.look: A village enclosed by woven bamboo fences, baskets and mats drying in every yard.
prov_r4_19_village_1.lore: Its people weave bamboo goods and sell them at Cổ Độ. The bamboo here is the first of the south, and the villagers cut only stems older than three years.

prov_r4_19_spirit_vein_2.name: Thanh Hư Mạch
prov_r4_19_spirit_vein_2.look: A still grove of pine and bamboo on a high slope, where no wind moves the leaves.
prov_r4_19_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi rises in the grove, and the stillness helps cultivators empty their minds. Vạn Hác's students come to rest their ears.

prov_r4_2_village_1.name: Liệp Hồ Thôn
prov_r4_2_village_1.look: A northern village of log houses, fox pelts stretched on every wall.
prov_r4_2_village_1.lore: Its hunters trap foxes and fish the coast in summer. They pay the grey wolves a share of every winter's catch by leaving carcasses on the knoll.

prov_r4_2_beast_lair_2.name: Thương Lang Cương
prov_r4_2_beast_lair_2.look: A forested knoll with wolf trails worn into the moss and bones scattered at its foot.
prov_r4_2_beast_lair_2.lore: Grey wolves den here and hunt the forest and tundra. The fox hunters leave them carcasses each winter to keep the peace.

prov_r4_20_village_1.name: Bán Sơn Thôn
prov_r4_20_village_1.look: A village of stone houses halfway up a forested mountain, terraced herb beds below it.
prov_r4_20_village_1.lore: It lives by goats, herbs and the disciples who climb to the peak. Its people guide them up for a fee.

prov_r4_20_peak_2.name: Bích Lạc Phong
prov_r4_20_peak_2.look: A bare rock peak above the pines, its summit standing in clear blue sky above the clouds.
prov_r4_20_peak_2.lore: A peak of Metal qi rises over sixteen hundred metres here. Tùng Đào's disciples climb it in summer to temper their arts in its thin, cold air.

prov_r4_21_village_1.name: Vân Ổ Thôn
prov_r4_21_village_1.look: A village in a high hollow, often sunk in cloud, with goat pens and stone huts.
prov_r4_21_village_1.lore: Its villagers herd goats and gather mountain herbs. They can find their way in cloud by the sound of goat bells.

prov_r4_21_peak_2.name: Thúy Trâm Phong
prov_r4_21_peak_2.look: A slender, green-grey spire of rock rises above the forest like a hairpin thrust into the clouds.
prov_r4_21_peak_2.lore: A peak of Earth and Metal qi, its rock streaked with pale green. Climbers say it sings faintly in the wind, and the goat herders of Vân Ổ will not climb past its shoulder.

prov_r4_22_village_1.name: Lạc Thạch Thôn
prov_r4_22_village_1.look: A village of stone houses among boulders under the crags, millstones stacked by the road.
prov_r4_22_village_1.lore: Villagers quarry the stones that fall in spring and carve millstones. They remember Hàn Thạch Trấn.

prov_r4_22_forest_2.name: Thâm Vụ Lâm
prov_r4_22_forest_2.look: A high fir forest swallowed by mist most days, its trunks dripping.
prov_r4_22_forest_2.lore: The mist never lifts for long, and the villagers will not enter it without a rope. Mosses here are prized by alchemists.

prov_r4_22_ruin_3.name: Hàn Thạch Trấn
prov_r4_22_ruin_3.look: On a high mountain shelf, the roofs of a stone town poke out of a field of tumbled rock and old snow.
prov_r4_22_ruin_3.lore: A quarry town that cut stone for Tùng Đào's halls. In the winter of 1151 an avalanche buried it, and the survivors moved down to Lạc Thạch.

prov_r4_23_village_1.name: Thảo Pha Thôn
prov_r4_23_village_1.look: A village on a grassy slope, cattle grazing around it and yew bows drying under the eaves.
prov_r4_23_village_1.lore: Its people graze cattle and make yew bows. It is the warmest village in the pine sea.

prov_r4_23_forest_2.name: Tử Sam Lâm
prov_r4_23_forest_2.look: A dark wood of old yews with red, peeling bark and poisonous red berries.
prov_r4_23_forest_2.lore: The bowyers take only fallen branches. Cattle that stray in sicken from the berries.

prov_r4_24_village_1.name: Thạch Tỉnh Thôn
prov_r4_24_village_1.look: Stone houses with slab roofs ring a deep well cut through the rock, its rim worn smooth by ropes, and green-stained copper diggings scar the slope above.
prov_r4_24_village_1.lore: The village grew around the well, which has never run dry even in the drought years, and its people herd goats and dig a little copper ore for the smiths of Cổ Độ. Every family hangs a bell over the well on the night a child is born.

prov_r4_24_beast_lair_2.name: Phi Thử Nhai
prov_r4_24_beast_lair_2.look: A high crag above the forest where big furred shapes glide from ledge to ledge at dusk.
prov_r4_24_beast_lair_2.lore: Giant spirit flying squirrels nest in the crag and steal from the village stores. Villagers hang their food in sealed jars.

prov_r4_25_mine_1.name: Hôi Thiết Khoáng
prov_r4_25_mine_1.look: On a bare mountain slope, small mine mouths open in grey rock under the grey pines.
prov_r4_25_mine_1.lore: The mine digs grey iron ore from the high rock. Tùng Đào's watch on Thương Tùng Mạch guards it too.

prov_r4_26_village_1.name: Tửu Phường Thôn
prov_r4_26_village_1.look: A village of brewhouses and wine jars, the air sharp with pine.
prov_r4_26_village_1.lore: Its brewers make pine-needle wine and sell it on the road to Cổ Độ. The wine is said to taste of the wind in the pines.

prov_r4_26_beast_lair_2.name: Độc Phong Lâm
prov_r4_26_beast_lair_2.look: A wood humming with hornets, their paper nests hanging from the branches like lanterns.
prov_r4_26_beast_lair_2.lore: Venom hornets as long as a finger nest here. Alchemists pay well for their venom.

prov_r4_27_village_1.name: Quan Hạ Thôn
prov_r4_27_village_1.look: A village of stone houses under the broken walls of Thiết Tỏa Quan.
prov_r4_27_village_1.lore: Its people herd goats and work the iron mine above. They guide Tùng Đào's elders and disciples to the fort.

prov_r4_27_peak_2.name: Đoạn Liên Phong
prov_r4_27_peak_2.look: A bare peak above the fort, from which the river road can be seen far below.
prov_r4_27_peak_2.lore: A peak of Metal qi, named for the chain that broke below it in 508. Tùng Đào's elders bring disciples to its summit to look down at the river.

prov_r4_27_mine_3.name: Tỏa Thiết Khoáng
prov_r4_27_mine_3.look: On a high slope, black spoil heaps run down from a timbered adit, and rusted ore carts lie where the old track ends.
prov_r4_27_mine_3.lore: The mine digs dark iron ore; old miners say iron from here went into the chain of Thiết Tỏa Quan, which gave the mine its name. It is worked again today by the people of Quan Hạ.

prov_r4_3_village_1.name: Thủ Mộ Thôn
prov_r4_3_village_1.look: A quiet village at the edge of an old temple's graveyard, its people sweeping the stones.
prov_r4_3_village_1.lore: Its villagers keep the graves of Khô Mộc Tự and gather firewood and fungus. They were the temple's servants once.

prov_r4_3_forest_2.name: Tịch Tĩnh Lâm
prov_r4_3_forest_2.look: A still pine forest where the wind seems to stop at the edge.
prov_r4_3_forest_2.lore: Birdsong carries for a mile here. The monks of Khô Mộc Tự meditated among its trees.

prov_r4_3_ruin_3.name: Khô Mộc Tự
prov_r4_3_ruin_3.look: In the forest, the halls of a temple stand roofless around a huge dead tree, grey and bare.
prov_r4_3_ruin_3.lore: A small sect that cultivated the stillness of withered wood. In 641 its abbot's art turned on him and he withered with his tree; his monks scattered, and the village kept the graves.

prov_r4_4_village_1.name: Hắc Nhĩ Thôn
prov_r4_4_village_1.look: A damp village where logs stacked by the houses are crusted with dark wood-ear fungus, and baskets of it dry on the eaves.
prov_r4_4_village_1.lore: Its people grow and gather black wood-ear fungus on fallen logs. Their dried fungus is sold at Tùng Gian Thành, and the best of it goes up to the palace kitchens.

prov_r4_4_forest_2.name: Lục Vân Lâm
prov_r4_4_forest_2.look: A misty green forest where moss hangs from every branch.
prov_r4_4_forest_2.lore: The fungus gatherers find their best logs here. It is green and misty even in late autumn.

prov_r4_5_village_1.name: Tùng Hoa Thôn
prov_r4_5_village_1.look: A village whose roofs turn yellow with pollen each spring, and cloths spread to catch it.
prov_r4_5_village_1.lore: Villagers collect pine pollen for cakes and medicine. Tùng Đào's alchemists buy most of it.

prov_r4_5_spirit_vein_2.name: Thúy Ba Mạch
prov_r4_5_spirit_vein_2.look: Rolling green hills where the pines ripple like waves in the wind.
prov_r4_5_spirit_vein_2.lore: A spirit vein of Wood qi runs under the hills. Tùng Đào's disciples cultivate here in spring.

prov_r4_6_town_1.name: Mộc Tập Trấn
prov_r4_6_town_1.look: A river town of timber yards and log ponds, its wharves stacked with marked logs.
prov_r4_6_town_1.lore: The timber of the north is gathered here and sold at a fair each spring. Tùng Đào's foresters check every brand.

prov_r4_6_forest_2.name: Thủy Sam Lâm
prov_r4_6_forest_2.look: A grove of tall dawn redwoods along the river, their feathery needles turning red in autumn.
prov_r4_6_forest_2.lore: These trees grow only by the river and are protected by the foresters. Their wood is light and floats well.

prov_r4_7_town_1.name: Lâu Thuyền Trấn
prov_r4_7_town_1.look: A coastal town of shipyards and slipways, half-built hulls rising like ribs.
prov_r4_7_town_1.lore: It builds Tùng Đào's coastal ships and Lãng Đào's sea-going barges. Its shipwrights are the best in the north.

prov_r4_7_forest_2.name: Trực Cán Lâm
prov_r4_7_forest_2.look: A forest of tall, straight pines like ship masts.
prov_r4_7_forest_2.lore: The mast pines are guarded by foresters and cut only for the shipyards. A crooked tree here is a rare sight.

prov_r4_8_village_1.name: Thải Tân Thôn
prov_r4_8_village_1.look: A plain village with firewood stacked along every road.
prov_r4_8_village_1.lore: Its villagers gather firewood and sell it to the coast towns. They are proud of their plain lives.

prov_r4_8_forest_2.name: Tạp Mộc Lâm
prov_r4_8_forest_2.look: A rolling wood where pines stand among oak, birch and maple, the floor deep in acorns and broad fallen leaves.
prov_r4_8_forest_2.lore: The firewood gatherers of Thải Tân take its deadwood, and its acorns fatten the wild boar that the villagers hunt each autumn. Tùng Đào's foresters leave it unmarked, since its timber is too crooked for ships or halls.

prov_r4_9_village_1.name: Triều Thanh Thôn
prov_r4_9_village_1.look: A fishing village of grey roofs by the sea.
prov_r4_9_village_1.lore: Its fishers listen to the tide to know when to sail. The sea wind bends the pines around it.

prov_r4_9_forest_2.name: Hải Phong Lâm
prov_r4_9_forest_2.look: On the low coast, a pine forest stands bent inland by the wind, its seaward trees dwarfed and salt-burned and its inner trees tall and straight.
prov_r4_9_forest_2.lore: The fishers of Triều Thanh read the weather by the sound of the wind in its crowns, and they gather pine pitch here to caulk their boats. Its windbreak keeps the salt off the village gardens.
